author: Nancy Burns-Fusaro Sun staff writer
title: Westerly Historical Society's regional 'History Fair' to take place at the Westerly Armory
text:
WESTERLY — Saturday's History Fair the Westerly Armory sponsored by the Westerly Historical Society — years in the making — is shaping up to be a blockbuster of an event.
Tom Gulluscio, president of the society, said he knew he was on to something a few years back when he asked representatives from local historical societies if they'd be interested in teaming up with the society for a sort of "history fair" at the Westerly Library.
"The response was overwhelming," said Gulluscio. "It was extremely well received."
Gulluscio said the Terrace Room of the library was filled with more than 22 organizations and more enthusiastic history lovers than he could count.
"It was astounding," he said Tuesday afternoon as he described 2022's "Regional History Fair." "It was absolutely great."
Ever since, he said, people have been asking if the society would organize another, similar fair.
The time has finally come. Saturday's free event at the Westerly Armory will feature representatives from more than 45 historical groups, societies, associations and museums who are prepared to set up information tables and greet the public.
Complementary light refreshments will be provided, Gulluscio said.
Under the guidance of Co-chairs Bob Peacock and Becky Jacoinski, the society has spent nearly a year working on the 2025 fair.
Gulluscio said since Roberta Mudge Humble — president of Westerly Armory Restoration, Inc. — had already contacted the society about the armory's 125th anniversary, it seemed natural to ask her if the fair could take place at the armory.
Gulluscio said Saturday's event will also serve as an kick off the armory's anniversary albeit a "tad early." It's a perfect time, he said, with so many "like-minded organizations" all together giving "a real testament to the great work that we all do to preserve, record and educate others about our storied past!"
The armory is providing the venue and the Westerly Historical Society is doing the "logistics of planning," and will provide food for the guests and refreshments for the public, Gulluscio said.
"The Westerly Armory is the perfect place to host 45 museums and historical societies from Rhode Island and nearby Connecticut," Humble said in an email Tuesday afternoon.
With no admission fee, the fair "will showcase the numerous historical societies, associations, and museums in the surrounding region," Gulluscio said, "and will allow a unique opportunity for the public to meet and greet members of these various organizations while learning about their membership opportunities."
Gulluscio said he asked each organization to bring along "some of their favorite treasured artifacts," to display and serve as conversation starters for their groups.
Some of the organizations planning to attend include historical societies from Charlestown, Quonochontaug, Hopkinton, Jamestown, Exeter, Richmond, Narragansett, Warwick, Babcock-Smith House Museum, the Beavertail Lighthouse Museum, Westerly Fire Department, Providence Family History Center, Westerly Memorial Library, South County History Center, Clouds Hill Victorian House, Tomaquag Museum, Westerly Vet's Fire Association, Living Sharks Museum and the hosts, Westerly Armory Museum Westerly Historical Society.
Some of the Connecticut organizations planning to attend include historical societies from Stonington, North Stonington, Noank, Ledyard and Preston, the Groton Family History Center, Stanton Davis Museum, Old Mystic History Center, Stonington Lighthouse Museum and Mystic River Historical Society.
"I really like this event because those who come may find other places to visit," said Humble. "We all look for day trips to new places and certainly Rhode Island, especially has a history unmatched."
The free event will take place Saturday, Oct. 25 from 1 to 4 p.m. at the Westerly Armory, Railroad Avenue, Westerly.
